source_text: In nobis uero sic unanimitas deminuta est, ut et largitas operationis infracta est. domos tunc et fundos uenundabant et thesauros sibi in caelo reponentes distribuenda in usus indigentium pretia apostolis offerebant. at nunc de patrimonio nec decimas damus et cum uendere iubeat Dominus, emimus potius et augemus. sic in nobis emarcuit uigor fidei, sic credentium robur elanguit. et idcirco Dominus tempora nostra respiciens in euangelio suo dicit: filius hominis cum uenerit, putas inueniet fidem in terra? uidemus fieri quod ille praedixit. in Dei timore, in lege iustitiae, in dilectione, in opere fides nulla est. nemo futurorum metum cogitat, diem Domini et iram Dei et incredulis uentura supplicia et statuta perfidis aeterna tormenta nemo considerat. quicquid metueret conscientia nostra, si crederet, quia non credit, omnino nec metuit. si autem crederet, et caueret: si caueret, et euaderet.
thought_title: Faith grown cold in the present age
orientation: Cyprian is contrasting the fervent unanimity and generosity of the apostolic Church with the weakened faith of his own time, before urging his readers to wake from spiritual sloth.
pass_a_gloss: In us [but] so [much] unanimity [has been] diminished, that also [the] generosity of working [good deeds] [has been] broken. houses then and lands they were selling and treasures for themselves in heaven storing [up], [the] prices to be distributed into [the] uses of [the] needy to [the] apostles they were offering. but now from [our] patrimony not even tithes we give and when [He] commands [us] to sell, [the] Lord, we buy rather and increase [our property]. so in us [has] withered [the] vigor of faith, so [the] strength of believers [has] grown weak. and therefore [the] Lord [upon] our times looking in His gospel says: [the] son of man when He [shall have] come, do you think He will find faith on [the] earth? we see [it] happening what He foretold. in [the] fear of God, in [the] law of justice, in love, in work faith [is] none. no one [of] future [things] [the] fear thinks [about], [the] day of [the] Lord and [the] wrath of God and to unbelievers [about] to come punishments and [the] established for [the] faithless eternal torments no one considers. whatever would fear our conscience, if it believed, because it does not believe, entirely not does it fear. but if it believed, also it would beware: if it were wary, also it would escape.

choices.why: Keeps the literal force of largitas as generous giving and operationis as active good work, matching Cyprian's contrast between apostolic charity and present stinginess.

choices.english: for the needs of the poor
choices.why: Indigentium means those in want; rendering as 'the poor' is plain and literal while preserving the sense of need.
rejected: for the uses of the needy
for the use of the indigent

choices.english: we do not even give tithes from our patrimony
choices.why: Patrimonium is inherited estate or family property; 'patrimony' is the exact English cognate and keeps the legal-economic sense.
rejected: from our inheritance we do not give tithes
from our estate we do not even give tenths

choices.english: the vigor of faith has withered
choices.why: Emarcesco is a strong verb of withering or fading; 'has withered' preserves the botanical metaphor Cyprian uses for spiritual decline.
rejected: the strength of faith has faded
the force of faith has drooped

choices.english: the punishments that are to come upon the unbelieving
choices.why: Incredulis is dative plural of those who do not believe; 'upon the unbelieving' keeps the dative of disadvantage and the future force of uentura.
rejected: the coming punishments for the incredulous

choices.english: the eternal torments appointed for the faithless
choices.why: Statuta is perfect passive participle of statuo, meaning established or appointed; 'appointed for the faithless' preserves the passive and the dative perfidis.
rejected: the eternal torments established for the treacherous
the fixed eternal torments for the perfidious

bible_refs.note: filius hominis cum uenerit, putas inueniet fidem in terra

pass_b_english: But among us this unanimity has so diminished that the generosity of good work has also been broken. Back then they used to sell houses and lands, and they offered the proceeds to the apostles to be distributed for the needs of the poor, storing up treasure for themselves in heaven. But now we do not even give tithes from our patrimony, and although the Lord commands us to sell, we instead buy and increase our holdings. So the vigor of faith has withered among us; so the strength of believers has grown weak. And therefore the Lord, looking upon our times, says in his Gospel: "When the Son of Man comes, do you think he will find faith on earth?" (Luke 18:8). We see happening what he foretold. There is no faith in the fear of God, in the law of justice, in love, in good work. No one thinks about the fear of things to come; no one considers the day of the Lord, the wrath of God, the punishments that are to come upon the unbelieving, and the eternal torments appointed for the faithless. Whatever our conscience would fear if it believed, it does not fear at all because it does not believe. But if it believed, it would also be on guard; if it were on guard, it would also escape.

last_rejected.why: operatio means active works/deeds, not 'work' as labor; 'good work' singular misrepresents the Latin plural sense of charitable deeds.
last_rejected.ruling: 'operatio' means work/deeds; 'good work' is within normal range. Singular vs plural is minor preference, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: Whatever our conscience would fear if it believed, it does not fear at all because it does not believe
last_rejected.source_quote: quicquid metueret conscientia nostra, si crederet, quia non credit, omnino nec metuit
last_rejected.why: The English inverts the causal logic: Latin says 'whatever our conscience would fear if it believed, because it does not believe, it does not fear at all.' The English 'because it does not believe' attaches to the wrong clause, making it sound like the explanation for why it would fear, rather than why it doesn't fear.
last_rejected.fix: Whatever our conscience would fear if it believed—because it does not believe, it does not fear at all
last_rejected.ruling: English 'it does not fear at all because it does not believe' correctly renders 'quia non credit, omnino nec metuit'; causal logic is preserved.
